name: Denali (Mount McKinley)
displayDescription: Alaska Native Athabaskan lands; fierce subarctic storms and massive relief make Denali a legendary undertaking.

name: Mount Saint Elias (US–Canada)

name: Mount Foraker
displayDescription: In the central Alaska Range; culturally tied to Denali expeditions with big, cold alpine faces.

name: Mount Bona

name: Mount Blackburn
displayDescription: Vast icefields and remote access; weather and isolation boost the commitment.

name: Mount Wrangell
displayDescription: Active shield volcano; rolling icefields where weather and crevasses test parties.

name: Mount Fairweather (US–Canada)
displayDescription: Named for rare clear days; coastal storms and glaciation make it anything but fair.

name: Mount Whitney
displayDescription: On Paiute land; highest in the Lower 48, with a strong Sierra hiking culture and strict permit system.

name: Mount Rainier

name: Mount Elbert

name: Mount Massive
displayDescription: Rival to Elbert; high, broad ridges with typical Colorado 14er culture.

name: Mount Harvard
displayDescription: Collegiate Peaks namesake; long but non-technical for experienced hikers.

name: Pikes Peak

name: Longs Peak

name: Mount Blue Sky (Mount Evans)

name: Quandary Peak

name: Capitol Peak
displayDescription: Knife-edge ridges and loose rock: a rite of passage in the Elk Range.

name: Maroon Peak (Maroon Bells)
displayDescription: ‘Deadly Bells’ shale; gorgeous but infamous for rock quality and route-finding.

name: Mount Sneffels
displayDescription: San Juan gem; couloirs and wildflower basins with old mining-town heritage.

name: Mount Wilson
displayDescription: Complex ridge systems and lingering snow; Telluride’s rugged skyline.

name: Uncompahgre Peak
displayDescription: Broad San Juan summit with sweeping tundra; summer thunderstorms common.

name: San Luis Peak
displayDescription: Quiet La Garita Wilderness; solitude and afternoon storm timing define success.

name: Mount of the Holy Cross
displayDescription: Cross couloir snowfields inspire pilgrimages; fickle weather demands care.

name: Mount Democrat
displayDescription: Part of the ‘Decalibron’ circuit—a cultural loop of four 14ers in a day.

name: Mount Lincoln
displayDescription: Mining history underfoot; typical high alpine weather patterns.

name: Mount Bross
displayDescription: Access etiquette and private land considerations are part of the climb.

name: White Mountain Peak
displayDescription: Ancient bristlecones and a high, dry Great Basin feel with road-adjacent routes.

name: Mount Shasta
displayDescription: Karuk land; glaciated volcano with revered spiritual significance and steep spring snow.

name: Mount Hood
displayDescription: Wy’east in local tradition; crevasse rescues and early-morning summit culture.

name: Mount Jefferson (Oregon)
displayDescription: Remote glaciers and volcanic spires; fewer crowds than Hood, more objective hazard.

name: Glacier Peak
displayDescription: One of the most remote Cascade volcanoes; long approaches through wild valleys.

name: Mount Baker
displayDescription: Kulshan’s icefall routes are a rite of passage for PNW alpinists.

name: Mount Adams
displayDescription: Large, glaciated but with mellow standard routes; corn skiing culture.

name: Mount St. Helens
displayDescription: A living geology classroom; permits and volcano monitoring shape the experience.

name: Mount Olympus (WA)
displayDescription: Hoh Rain Forest approaches and coastal weather create a uniquely wild climb.

name: Half Dome
displayDescription: Ahwahneechee homeland; cables-route permits and granite big-wall culture.

name: El Capitan
displayDescription: Global center of big-wall culture; technical rock expertise and multi-day systems.

name: Lassen Peak
displayDescription: Active in historic times; classic spring snow routes and national-park education.

name: Telescope Peak
displayDescription: Death Valley’s rooftop: extreme temperature swings and vast desert views.

name: Mount San Jacinto
displayDescription: Cahuilla land; cable car approaches meet alpine granite traditions.

name: San Gorgonio Mountain
displayDescription: SoCal’s high point; snow travel in winter contrasts with hot chaparral summers.

name: Mount San Antonio (Mt Baldy)
displayDescription: Weekend rite for LA hikers; winter ‘Baldy Bowl’ brings alpine skills into play.

name: Mauna Kea
displayDescription: Sacred to Native Hawaiians; thin air above the Pacific and observatory access complexities.

name: Mauna Loa
displayDescription: World’s largest shield volcano; long, hot lava fields and recent eruptions inform planning.

name: Haleakalā
displayDescription: House of the Sun; crater traverses and Hawaiian cultural stewardship.

name: Mount Waialeale
displayDescription: Among the wettest places on Earth; near-constant rain and mud make for serious travel.

name: Mount Washington
displayDescription: Abenaki lands; infamous for record winds and fast-changing weather.

name: Mount Mansfield
displayDescription: Green Mountain ridge-walk culture, alpine zones protected by local ethics.

name: Katahdin
displayDescription: Baxter State Park ethos; Knife Edge thrills and Appalachian Trail lore.

name: Mount Marcy
displayDescription: Adirondack High Peaks culture: rugged trails, lean-tos, and summit stewards.

name: Mount Mitchell
displayDescription: Highest east of the Mississippi; spruce-fir ecology and Blue Ridge Parkway access.

name: Clingmans Dome
displayDescription: Cherokee homeland; high humidity and frequent fog on the Appalachian spine.

name: Mount Rogers
displayDescription: High meadows, wild ponies nearby; gentle but often windy.

name: Black Elk Peak
displayDescription: Sacred to the Lakota; granite fire-lookout culture and rolling forests.

name: Borah Peak
displayDescription: Knife-edge Class 3 and big elevation gain; intermountain weather swings.

name: Gannett Peak
displayDescription: Wind River glaciers and long approaches—classic Western wilderness mountaineering.

name: Granite Peak (Montana)
displayDescription: Exposed scrambling, fickle storms, and remote routes in the Beartooths.

name: Kings Peak
displayDescription: High Uinta backcountry culture; long but non-technical with afternoon storm timing.

name: Mount Timpanogos
displayDescription: Beloved Wasatch classic; wildflower basins and lingering snowfields.

name: Humphreys Peak
displayDescription: San Francisco Peaks; monsoon lightning and wind exposure define summer ascents.

name: Guadalupe Peak
displayDescription: Chihuahuan Desert views; high winds common along exposed ridges.

name: Boundary Peak
displayDescription: Great Basin scree; often combined with Montgomery Peak across the border.

name: Wheeler Peak (New Mexico)
displayDescription: Taos Pueblo region; alpine lakes and summer thunder tradition.

name: Charleston Peak
displayDescription: Desert island of bristlecones above Las Vegas; fast weather shifts.

name: Mount Olympus (Utah)
displayDescription: Local Salt Lake rite; steep, rocky trails with big views over the valley.

name: Mount Hoodoo (proxy for Three Sisters area)
displayDescription: Volcanic Cascade culture—glacier travel skills and route-finding around tephra slopes.

name: Mount Washington (Oregon)
displayDescription: Classic Oregon volcano cone with crumbly rock and airy ridges.

name: Mount Shuksan
displayDescription: Photogenic North Cascades icon; complex glacier systems and alpine rock.

name: Mount Rainier Little Tahoma
displayDescription: Sharp sub-peak of Rainier with steep snow/ice—serious despite stature.

name: Mount Whitney (Mountaineer’s Route)

name: Mount Hood (North Side)
displayDescription: Icefall labyrinths and steeper gullies define the more technical faces.

name: Mount Everest
displayDescription: Chomolungma/Sagarmatha: high-altitude culture, Sherpa logistics, and jet-stream windows.

name: K2

name: Kangchenjunga
displayDescription: Sacred summit customs; traditionally stopping short out of respect in Sikkimese lore.

name: Lhotse
displayDescription: Linked to Everest’s Western Cwm; steep couloirs and thin air.

name: Makalu
displayDescription: Pyramid of ice and rock; remote approaches and fierce winds.

name: Cho Oyu
displayDescription: Considered one of the 'easier' 8000ers yet demands serious glacier travel.

name: Dhaulagiri I
displayDescription: Storm-battered ridges over deep Kali Gandaki; austere and avalanche-prone.

name: Manaslu
displayDescription: Popular 8000er with cultural circuits around Gurung villages.

name: Nanga Parbat
displayDescription: Dramatic relief above Indus Valley; notorious Rupal Face and weather.

name: Annapurna I
displayDescription: Steep, avalanche-loaded faces; name tied to both trekking culture and serious alpinism.

name: Aconcagua

name: Ojos del Salado
displayDescription: World’s highest volcano; Atacama logistics and bone-dry altitude.

name: Fitz Roy (Cerro Chaltén)

name: Cerro Torre
displayDescription: Rime ice mushrooms, fierce winds—an apex of modern alpinism.

name: Huascarán Sur
displayDescription: Quechua heartland; glacier collapse risks and high tropical snow.

name: Alpamayo
displayDescription: Perfect fluted faces; steep ice lines framed by Andean village culture.

name: Chimborazo
displayDescription: Closest summit to the Sun (equatorial bulge); cold, windy nights above paramo.

name: Cotopaxi
displayDescription: Active stratovolcano; glacier skills and Cotopaxi National Park traditions.

name: Pico de Orizaba (Citlaltépetl)

name: Popocatépetl
displayDescription: Active volcano with frequent closures; deeply woven into Mexica legend.

name: Iztaccíhuatl
displayDescription: ‘Sleeping Woman’; high-altitude hike over a series of false summits.

name: Kilimanjaro
displayDescription: Chagga porters and huts; rainforest-to-alpine desert in a single climb.

name: Mount Kenya (Batian)

name: Margherita Peak (Rwenzori)
displayDescription: ‘Mountains of the Moon’: boggy approaches and equatorial glaciers.

name: Mont Blanc
displayDescription: Birthplace of alpinism; tramways, refuges, and crevasse/serac hazards.

name: Matterhorn

name: Eiger

name: Jungfrau
displayDescription: Railway access meets glaciated terrain and classic Swiss hut culture.

name: Dufourspitze (Monte Rosa)

name: Elbrus
displayDescription: Cableways, snowcats, and brutal winds; a Seven Summits staple.

name: Mount Ararat
displayDescription: Sacred in Armenian tradition; high, cold volcanic dome.

name: Damavand
displayDescription: Fumaroles and Persian mountaineering clubs—classic summer ascent with sulfur whiffs.

name: Mount Elgon (Wagagai)
displayDescription: Extinct shield volcano with unique afro-alpine flora and cave traditions.

name: Mount Fuji
displayDescription: Pilgrimage routes, torii gates, and sunrise ‘Goraikō’ culture during the climbing season.
